samples.summary: The chip's new "turn on offline saving" offer is never clicked by any test
samples.evidence: The diff adds a whole interactive branch: when `offerOffline` is true the chip renders as a `<button onClick={turnOnOfflineSaving}>` (sync-status-chip.tsx:287-303) and the stranded toast gains `action: { label: 'Turn on for later documents', onClick: turnOnOfflineSaving }` (~line 238). `turnOnOfflineSaving` calls `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled(true)` and raises a success toast. The only new test in tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:418-446 reads `warning.mock.calls[0][1].action.label` and asserts wording — it never invokes the handler, never asserts the preference was written, never asserts a success toast, and never asserts the chip becomes a button (or stays a span when the device has already opted in / the build cannot honour it). A broken or unwired handler ships green: the user clicks the design's 'second entry point', nothing is persisted, and they go on believing un-sent work is on disk.

samples.summary: Nothing asserts the share route actually wraps itself in NonDurableScope
samples.evidence: `NonDurableScope` is the only thing keeping share-link content off a visitor's disk, and the code says so at length (use-durable-document.ts:44-60, collab-document-provider.tsx docs). The durable suite's case 'never persists anything reached through a share link' (src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx) applies `NonDurableScope` by hand in the test render — it proves the mechanism, not the wiring. A grep for `NonDurableScope` finds it only in use-durable-document.ts, shared-document.tsx, collab-document-provider.tsx and that one test; no test renders `SharedDocumentInner`/the shared route and asserts the scope is present. Delete the wrapper from shared-document.tsx and the whole suite stays green, while a signed-in visitor on somebody's share link gets the durable branch: their own `wb:{userId}:{docKey}` client on their personal Yorkie token, writing shared content to disk past the link's revocation.

samples.summary: The new Settings "Offline" section and its supportsClientKey() gate have no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds a gated section — `{offlineAvailable && (<section>… <Switch id="offline-switch" checked={offlineEnabled} onCheckedChange={setOfflinePersistenceEnabled} /> …)}`. There is no test file for this page anywhere: globbing `packages/frontend/**/*settings*` returns only `app/notes/notes-settings.ts`, `app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx` and its test, and grepping `Save documents on this device|offline-switch|app/settings` matches only page.tsx, App.tsx and the README. So neither the gate (the toggle must not appear on a build that cannot honour it, per the design's Rollout note) nor the switch wiring is covered; only the underlying preference module is tested. Failure mode is a toggle that promises storage and erasure the build cannot perform, or one that does not persist the choice.
searchedFor: grep 'app/settings|settings/page|Save documents on this device|offline-switch' in packages/frontend

samples.summary: The "Save a copy" toast action — the user's only route back to un-reconciled work — is never invoked
samples.evidence: `offerRecoverableWork` builds a toast whose action `onClick` calls `recoverOfflineCopy` and then branches over the outcome: three distinct `refused` messages, an incomplete-copy note, and an 'Open' action that calls `navigate(getDocumentPath(...))` (offline-runtime.tsx:188-229). src/components/offline-runtime.test.tsx only asserts the offer is *made* and explicitly that `recoverOfflineCopy` was **not** called ('offers work that could not be saved, without creating anything'); no test pulls `toastWarning.mock.calls[0][1].action.onClick` and runs it. `recoverOfflineCopy` itself is well covered, but the mapping from its outcomes to what the user sees, and the navigation, are untested — a broken handler leaves the archive permanently un-recoverable from the UI while the same toast reappears every session.

samples.summary: "stays lowered after a later write succeeds" never simulates a later write
samples.evidence: The case (durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:71-82) fires `captured[0].onWriteFailure?.(...)`, waits for 'not-durable', then sleeps 10ms and re-asserts 'not-durable'. The mocked `WafflebaseDocStore` is a class with only a constructor — there is no write method to succeed, and nothing in the test signals a successful write. The assertion therefore holds for any implementation where the flag is a `useState` that nothing resets, i.e. it cannot distinguish a latched flag from one that is merely never lowered by anything in scope. The named property (a later success does not restore durability) is not exercised.

samples.summary: Route-param encoding guard weakened from every request to some request
samples.evidence: The loop previously asserted, for every URL a call produced, both `pathname` not containing `/auth/logout` and `pathname` containing `encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)`. The diff keeps the first for all URLs but downgrades the second to `paths.some(...)`. The stated reason (deleteWorkspace now makes a companion listing request carrying no id) is legitimate, but the weaker form no longer catches a call where the id reaches *one* request encoded and another request interpolates it in a way that does not normalise to `/auth/logout` — the property the original loop pinned per-request. Worth narrowing to 'every request that mentions the id encodes it' rather than 'at least one does'.

samples.summary: The erase-watcher getter is checked only for being a function, not for what it returns
samples.evidence: 'installs the erase watcher and reads the identity at fire time' asserts `typeof storeOf === 'function'` and `userOf() === '42'`. The user getter is genuinely exercised; the store getter is not — `() => undefined` or a getter returning the wrong store would pass. Since `watchForOfflineDisable` falls back to constructing its own store when the getter yields nothing, a broken store getter is silent, and this is the only case asserting the wiring.

samples.summary: Nothing asserts PrivateRoute mounts OfflineRuntime with the signed-in id
samples.evidence: `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` is the single mount point for the erase watcher, the thirty-day sweep, the revoked-access reconcile and the recovery offer — the component's own doc says nothing else runs any of them. `OfflineRuntime`'s behaviour is tested in isolation (src/components/offline-runtime.test.tsx), but I found no test rendering `PrivateRoute` and asserting the runtime is mounted, or that it receives the identity. Removing the line leaves every offline test green while the housekeeping silently never runs.

samples.summary: Group-member connector case asserts the endpoint value it fed in
samples.evidence: 'keeps a connector attached to a group member' ends with `expect(connector.start.elementId).toBe('child-1')` — the same id supplied in the fixture, and the value an implementation that did no remapping at all would leave. The case is saved by `expect(result.droppedConnectors).toBe(0)` above it, which is the real signal; the endpoint assertion adds no discrimination and reads as coverage it is not providing.

finding.summary: The chip's new "turn on offline saving" offer is never clicked by any test
finding.evidence: The diff adds a whole interactive branch: when `offerOffline` is true the chip renders as a `<button onClick={turnOnOfflineSaving}>` (sync-status-chip.tsx:287-303) and the stranded toast gains `action: { label: 'Turn on for later documents', onClick: turnOnOfflineSaving }` (~line 238). `turnOnOfflineSaving` calls `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled(true)` and raises a success toast. The only new test in tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:418-446 reads `warning.mock.calls[0][1].action.label` and asserts wording — it never invokes the handler, never asserts the preference was written, never asserts a success toast, and never asserts the chip becomes a button (or stays a span when the device has already opted in / the build cannot honour it). A broken or unwired handler ships green: the user clicks the design's 'second entry point', nothing is persisted, and they go on believing un-sent work is on disk.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. sync-status-chip.tsx:146-158 adds turnOnOfflineSaving (writes setOfflinePersistenceEnabled(true) + success toast), :238-243 wires it as the stranded toast's action, and :287-301 renders the chip as a clickable <button> when offerOffline. The only test for this (tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:418-446) reads warning.mock.calls[0][1].action.label and asserts wording only — it never calls action.onClick, never asserts the preference was written, never asserts the success toast, and never asserts the button-vs-span rendering. Repo-wide grep for `action.onClick`/`action!.onClick`/`action?.onClick` (excluding node_modules) returns zero matches, so no test anywhere invokes a toast action handler; grep for turnOnOfflineSaving/offerOffline/'Turn on for later'/'Saving on this device is on' hits only the component and review-artifact JSON. Sibling suites (sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx, site-header-sync-status.test.tsx, shared-header-status.test.tsx) contain no offline-offer coverage, and there is no e2e directory. Existing setOfflinePersistenceEnabled tests cover the lib/Settings path, not the chip's wiring. A broken or unwired handler would ship green with a silent user-visible failure (user believes un-sent work is now durable), so the gap is major under the missing-tests lane.

finding.summary: `OfflineRuntime` — the whole housekeeping runtime — has no test of any kind
finding.evidence: Glob `packages/frontend/**/*offline-runtime*` returns only the source file; grep for `OfflineRuntime|offerRecoverableWork|rememberOfflineUser` across packages/frontend matches only offline-erase.ts/.test.ts (the helper), the component itself, and PrivateRoute.tsx. Nothing exercises: (a) `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` being called on mount — which is the *only* thing that makes `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` find an identity, so a regression here silently leaves document content on a shared device after sign-out while every offline-erase.test.ts case still passes (they call `rememberOfflineUser` themselves); (b) `watchForOfflineDisable(() => store, () => userId)` being installed at all, i.e. the Settings promise "turning it off deletes them"; (c) the once-per-session `collectStale()` sweep; (d) `offerRecoverableWork` — the loop that decides *not* to auto-create, skips keys `describeArchivedDocument` cannot read, dedupes by toast id, honours the `cancelled()` getter across awaits, and routes via `getDocumentPath`. The individual leaves (`recoverOfflineCopy`, `describeArchivedDocument`, `watchForOfflineDisable`) are well tested; the orchestration that actually invokes them on a real session is not.

verdict.reason: The finding's absence claim is factually wrong: packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.test.tsx exists (196 lines, 11 cases) and renders the real OfflineRuntime. It covers every behavior the finding names as untested: (a) rememberOfflineUser('42') on mount at test:99-102 plus the deliberate non-forgetting on unmount at test:186-194; (b) watchForOfflineDisable installed at test:111-121, asserting the two args are getters and userOf() === '42', matching offline-runtime.tsx:71-74, with teardown of stopWatching/close at test:177-184; (c) the once-per-session collectStale sweep at test:123-126 and continuation after a failed reconcile at test:146-152; (d) offerRecoverableWork at test:154-164 (offers without calling recoverOfflineCopy, title reaches the description) and test:166-174 (a docKey describeArchivedDocument cannot read produces no toast, covering offline-runtime.tsx:167-172), plus the 'never purge on a listing the server did not give' guard at test:128-144 against offline-runtime.tsx:114-116. Mocks are of collaborators, not the unit under test — the effect at offline-runtime.tsx:54-145 really runs, so the tests can fail. The file is executed by the runner: vite.config.ts:452-457 includes 'src/**/*.test.tsx'. Residual narrow gaps (toast-id dedupe, getDocumentPath routing, cancelled() mid-await) are not the filed finding and are not blocking alone.

finding.summary: The `eraseLocalData: false` guard on the 401 path — and `logout()`'s erase call — are untested
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/tests/api/auth.test.ts` only covers 401 redirect de-duplication (grep for `erase|offline|401` returns lines 4-56, all about the redirect burst); no test in the repo asserts that the 401 arm of `fetchWithAuth` passes `eraseLocalData: false`. The diff's own comment states this is load-bearing: an involuntary expiry must not delete "the archives that hold changes the server never took", which are by design the only remaining copy of unreconciled work. A regression flipping that default destroys user work on a routine cookie expiry, and nothing would fail. Symmetrically, no test asserts `logout()` awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` before redirecting, or that a failing erase cannot fail the sign-out — `offline-erase.test.ts` tests the helper in isolation, never the caller.

verdict.reason: Direct counterexamples exist in the very file the reviewer cites. `packages/frontend/tests/api/auth.test.ts` contains a second describe block, `sign-out and local data` (lines 81-152), which the finding overlooks: (a) lines 114-124 stub fetch to 401, call `fetchWithAuth`, and assert `expect(erase).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ keepArchives: true })` — this is exactly the assertion the finding says does not exist for the 401 arm, and it would fail if `auth.ts:266` were flipped to the `"all"` default, contradicting "nothing would fail"; (b) lines 102-112 assert `toHaveBeenCalledWith({ keepArchives: false })` for a deliberate `logout()`, covering the erase call at `auth.ts:125`; (c) lines 126-151 record an ordering array from the erase mock and the `window.location.href` setter and assert `['erase','redirect']`, covering the "awaits erase before redirecting" property the finding says is untested. The tests genuinely run: `vite.config.ts:450-458` sets `environment: 'jsdom'` and includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`. This is not over-mocking either — only `offline-erase.ts` is mocked (auth.test.ts:87-90) while the unit under test (auth.ts option selection) is real, and the helper itself is covered in `src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts:252-320`. The finding also references a non-existent `eraseLocalData: false` shape; the code uses a `"all" | "keep-archives"` union (auth.ts:34). Only a narrow sub-claim survives (no test that a rejecting erase cannot fail sign-out), which is an uncovered edge case, not the stated major gap.

finding.summary: `removeMember`'s `isOfflineUser` cross-account guard and `deleteWorkspace`'s pre-delete listing have no tests
finding.evidence: Grep for `isOfflineUser|documentIdsIn` across packages/frontend matches only `lib/offline-erase.ts` and `api/workspaces.ts` — no test file. There is no `api/workspaces.test.ts` (Glob `packages/frontend/**/workspaces*.test.ts*` finds nothing; `app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-settings.test.tsx` is a component test). The guard the code documents at length — an owner removing *somebody else* must purge nothing, because the store is scoped to whoever is signed in on this device — is exactly the kind of inverted condition that deletes this user's local copies (including unsent work) of documents they still have every right to read, with no visible symptom. Likewise nothing pins that `documentIdsIn` is called *before* the access-ending DELETE, which is the only reason the purge can find anything.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that no `api/workspaces.test.ts` exists and that the `removeMember` guard and `deleteWorkspace` listing are untested — is false in this working tree. `packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.test.ts` exists (found via unfiltered Grep for `isOfflineUser|documentIdsIn` and Glob `**/workspaces*`; the reviewer's path-filtered searches evidently missed it) and contains non-vacuous tests for both behaviors. The cross-account guard is tested at workspaces.test.ts:130-144: with `isOfflineUser` returning false it asserts `fetchDocuments` was never called and that purge received `[]` — an inverted condition at workspaces.ts:160 would make both assertions fail, which is precisely the defect the finding says nothing would catch. The positive branch is at :111-128, including the `String(userId)` coercion. `deleteWorkspace`'s listing is covered at :50-68 (pins the slug-vs-id resolution that workspaces.ts:101-115 documents as the silent no-op, filtering out the `workspaceId: "other"` doc), :70-79 (id spelling), :81-88 (listing failure must not fail the delete), and :90-107 (no purge when the DELETE 403s, pinning purge after assertOk). The mocked symbols are real exports (offline-erase.ts:102, :226) and the file is in vitest's include globs (vite.config.ts:452-457), so it genuinely runs; the mocking stops at the network boundary while the branch logic under test is real code. The only surviving residue is that the fetch mocks are order-independent, so a reordering of `documentIdsIn` after the DELETE would not fail a test — a far narrower point than the filed claim of total absence, and not blocking on its own.

finding.summary: No test that `deleteDocuments` purges only server-confirmed ids, or that `deleteDocument` purges only on `ok`
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts` line 133-145 is the only `deleteDocuments` case; it mocks `okJson({ deleted: ['a'] })` and asserts the URL, method, body and returned value — nothing about `purgeOfflineDocuments`. Line 112 calls `deleteDocument` purely to check id encoding. So the rule the diff added and justifies in a comment — purge only what the server reports deleted, because "dropping the local copy of a document that is still there would delete unsent work the user can still push" — has zero coverage. A regression to `purgeOfflineDocuments(ids)` (the requested ids) on a partial-failure response silently destroys unsent local work and the suite stays green.

verdict.reason: The claimed coverage gap does not exist. documents.test.ts mocks @/lib/offline-erase (line 5) and asserts the exact rule twice. For deleteDocuments, the test "drops the local copy of only what the server says it deleted" (lines 152-159) requests ["a","b"], mocks a partial server reply okJson({deleted:["a"]}), and asserts purgeOfflineDocuments was called with ["a"] — precisely the regression the finding describes (purging the requested ids) would pass ["a","b"] and fail this test. Two further cases cover deleted:[] (161-165) and a response with no deleted list (167-171), exercising the `?? []` at documents.ts:215. For deleteDocument, "keeps the local copy when the deletion was refused" (186-197) mocks {ok:false,status:403}, asserts the call rejects, and asserts purgeOfflineDocuments was NOT called — covering the `if (response.ok)` guard at documents.ts:162-172; the ok path is covered at 180-184. The assertions are neither vacuous nor over-mocked: purgeOfflineDocuments is a collaborator of the unit under test (documents.ts), and the tests assert the specific argument values that encode the rule, not merely that a mock was invoked. The finding's stated evidence ("line 133-145 is the only deleteDocuments case", grep for purgeOffline came up empty) is contradicted by the file, which runs to line 199.
